subject: Partner evidence exchange: govcompliance connector & attestation protocol
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@govcomply.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Partner evidence exchange: govcompliance connector & attestation protocol

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we'd like to formalize the evidence handoff pattern for GovComply customers that will use the Redwood private connector:

Key asks from our side:
- Supported evidence transport: SFTP push OR secure API ingestion to GovComply's "evidence intake" endpoint.
- File naming standard: <company>-<control>-<YYYYMMDD>-<tool>.zip (see attached template).
- Minimum metadata: control id, evidence type, collection timestamp, originating pipeline id.
- Proof-of-delivery: GovComply should return a signed receipt (JSON) for each bundle.

Attached: RDW-SOC2-Scope-Template.xlsx and a draft connector spec (govcomply-connector-spec.md). Can you confirm whether the signed receipt is already supported? If not, what minimal changes are needed on your side?

Timeline: Customer pilots start 2026-09-20. Prefer a small alpha connector + SFTP fallback by 2026-09-10.

Thanks — I looped in Laura for legal/contract questions.

Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya@govcomply.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: GovComply Integrations <integrations@govcomply.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@auditbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner evidence exchange: govcompliance connector & attestation protocol

Sergio —

Appreciate the clear spec. Quick answers:

- Signed receipt: GovComply supports a receipt ACK over our API today; it is a lightweight JSON with receipt_id, timestamp, sha256. We can extend it to include collector id.
- SFTP: supported. We have a hardened dropzone. See attached upload-instructions-sftp.txt.
- File naming / metadata: we can validate filename patterns on ingest and surface a validation_error webhook if anything fails.

Operational considerations:
- We will need to exchange SSH host keys for the SFTP flow and set a max retention window (we usually keep ingress bundles for 30 days unless the customer requests longer).
- For the API ingestion we need a mutual-TLS setup for production. We can accept API tokens for alpha.

We can commit a small alpha connector that accepts SFTP bundles + returns an ACK JSON by 2026-09-08. For mutual-TLS push, estimate 3 weeks of engineering post-alpha.

Tom (cc'd) — if AuditBridge is in scope for collection validation, will you need anything different from the receipt payload to tie into your evidence chain?

Regards,
Priya Shah
Head of Integrations, GovComply Solutions
priya@govcomply.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@govcomply.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner evidence exchange: govcompliance connector & attestation protocol

Thanks Priya —

A couple of legal/security guardrails from our side:
1) Retention: Redwood's customers may request longer retention; we need GovComply to support retention policy flags in the receipt or a per-bundle metadata field.
2) Access controls: Any evidence pulled into GovComply must be scoped to the customer's account; please confirm tenant isolation on your side.
3) Evidence provenance: We require an immutable audit id that maps to the originating Redwood request (collector id). The SHA in the ACK is fine but we also need a signed timestamp (or signed receipt) for higher-assurance customers.

Can you confirm whether GovComply's ACK JSON can include an optional fields: retention_policy, tenant_id, signed_receipt (base64)? If there are additional compliance costs for signed receipts we may need to discuss a cost pass-through for enterprise customers.

Also copying Vivek for a quick ops feasibility check and to confirm that our SFTP host keys are ready to be shared (we have a ticket with infra).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations (contracts), Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@govcomply.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner evidence exchange: govcompliance connector & attestation protocol

Priya —

Quick ops update from infra/engineering:
- SSH keys: We will provision a dedicated service keypair for GovComply. Please send your public host key and preferred SFTP username. We'll place the key in the RDW ingress ACL.
- Retention flags: Engineering can surface a retention_policy field on the bundle metadata; that field will be honored for reads/exports. Works for API and SFTP.
- Signed receipts: We can support a signed_receipt field if GovComply returns a JSON Web Signature (JWS) over the receipt payload. That matches our verification stack. If GovComply cannot sign, we can accept HMAC-based receipts but will mark them as lower assurance in our UI.

Acceptance criteria for alpha (target 2026-09-08):
- SFTP transfer succeeds and GovComply returns ACK JSON with receipt_id and sha256.
- GovComply provides a test receipt for one sample bundle (we will validate hash and retention fields).
- Both sides exchange contact points for incidents and broken ingest (Ops Slack + escalation email).

Next steps: Priya, can you share the SFTP host key and a sample ACK JSON? We'll send our host key by EOD today. If possible please attach the sample ACK and an example bundle by 2026-08-28 so we can run an end-to-end test in our staging environment.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
